key_insight: HSImul3R closes the perception–simulation gap by running physics in the loop: it jointly optimizes visual reconstruction and physical plausibility so human–scene reconstructions are both visually accurate and stable in simulators.
problem_solved: Existing 3D reconstructions of human–scene interactions look plausible visually but violate physical constraints (contacts, collisions, dynamics), causing instability or failure when used in physics engines and embodied AI tasks.
method: Physics-in-the-loop, bi-directional optimization that alternates between perception-driven reconstruction and simulator-driven physical refinement.
Joint estimation of geometry, human pose, contacts, and physical parameters so outputs are simulation-ready rather than only visually plausible.
Designed to work from casual captures (sparse-view images and monocular video) with constraints that enforce stability in downstream physics engines.
impact: Makes reconstructed human–scene scenes usable in robotics, virtual testing, and embodied AI by ensuring stability and realistic interactions in simulators; reduces manual cleanup and improves transfer to physics-driven applications.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing perception → reconstruction → physics simulator → feedback loop (bi-directional optimization).
Side-by-side before/after comparisons: visually plausible but physically invalid vs. simulation-ready stable reconstruction.
Contact and force overlay on a scene to illustrate detected/optimized contact points and physical parameters.
Chart of downstream stability metrics (e.g., simulation rollouts, contact energy, failure rate) comparing baseline vs HSImul3R.
paper_title: HSImul3R: Physics-in-the-Loop Reconstruction of Simulation-Ready Human-Scene Interactions
paper_authors: Yukang Cao, Haozhe Xie, Fangzhou Hong, Long Zhuo, Zhaoxi Chen
